output.brief: The 26-point gap mostly reflects who gets into Bridge Hours, not what the program does. District rules send every student below the 40th percentile on the fall test into it. Participants averaged 182.8 in the fall against 215.1 for everyone else, so they started about 32 points behind. When the research office compared students with similar fall scores, the winter gaps shrank to under one point, some positive and some negative. Northgate's claim of faster growth is also mostly a pattern seen in all low scorers, so it doesn't show the program works. The evidence neither supports ending the program nor shows it helps. I'm fairly sure of this, though the effect of the program itself is still unknown. Next steps: replace the raw chart with the matched comparison, and ask for the research office's cut-score comparison due 27 Feb. Link attendance to scores, and have the math coordinator observe sessions and check the fraction lessons against the classroom sequence. Don't end the contract now, don't expand it, and don't open sign-up to everyone. That last change would remove the referral list that gives the district a fair comparison. Revisit the decision once the better comparison is in.
